 Al-Ittihad coach after the slap from Al-Ain: we are not machines to switch at the push of a button!
 Originally posted on
 Goal.com 
  | 
 Last updated Nov 2, 2026 4:23 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 First comment from the manager after the Zamalek shock 
 Jens Wiesing refused to buckle after Al-Ittihad's heavy 4-1 defeat to Al-Ain of the UAE in the fourth round of the AFC Champions League Elite. The German coach insisted his team remained a work in progress, and that reaching the level the fans crave takes time and constant effort, not a change delivered at the press of a button.
 Wiesing stood by his players in the post-match press conference despite the harsh scoreline. "I am very happy with the players in my team, and I will defend them to the last breath," he said. "This is the same team that began the pre-season preparation period with us, but what has happened from the start of preparation until today? We have developed, and we are not machines to be transformed at the press of a button."
 Rough patches come with the territory when you are building a side, the German added. "It is natural to go through difficult days, but we are working day by day and week after week in order to develop. The fans deserve the best, the club deserves that, and we have a great deal of work ahead of us. Unfortunately, results alone are what judge the work of coaches, and sometimes the results are unjust."
 Vicing: the team cannot be judged on a single night
 Al-Ittihad's coach reflected on a painful night against Al-Ain, insisting that one off performance cannot wipe out everything his players had shown in previous games. "It was a difficult night, and a dip in level can happen. How many times have we been behind and come back in the result? The latest was the match against Neftçi. And how many times have the players shown the spirit of the tiger? I would be unjust to the team if I judged it based only on what it delivered today," he said.
 There's a long road ahead in the competition, Vesić stressed, and his side must sharpen several areas, particularly the mental and physical sides, if they want to go toe to toe with strong opponents. A bright start to the season, he pointed out, never meant the team was flawless.
 "If we want to compete, we have to be better. The preparation phase was good, and the results at the start were good too, but some people did not want to see the mistakes when we were winning, even though we were spotting them and working to correct them. What is happening now is part of the development phase, and this is not an excuse, because I do not make excuses," he explained.
 Read also.. Video: Al-Ain gives Al-Ittihad a taste of the Al-Nassr defeat in the AFC Champions League Elite
 Fixture congestion and fatigue: do they explain the collapse?
 The German coach highlighted the gulf in preparation time between the two sides. Al-Ain had a full week to get ready. Al-Ittihad had just three days, with fixtures piling up and the physical toll mounting.
 Vissing said: "Al-Ain had a week to prepare, while we had only three days. Since my arrival, I have seen development in the team, and we have played 18 matches, so managing loads and effort has become extremely important. Small mistakes affect the team, and we must focus on recovery and recuperation, as we still have a great deal of work ahead of us."
 His team, he added, must keep working to match their rivals physically and mentally. The development is far from finished. Al-Ittihad, he stressed, are only at the start of the journey towards the level they are chasing.
 I take responsibility: the defeat was not due to tactics
 Vesing defended his players but insisted he carries full responsibility for the results, even as he refused to accept the defeat to Al Ain as proof of a tactical flaw. He said: "As a coach, I take 100% of the responsibility. In every match that doesn't go well, I take responsibility, and I don't need to repeat that every time."
 "When the team starts the match correctly, you can't say the tactics were wrong," he added. "What happened today was not because of the tactics, but it was a night in the AFC Champions League, and we were facing a strong team with great experience in the tournament. We have to be present in all the details and know how to deal with these circumstances."
 Restoring Al-Ittihad to their former standing will take time, Vesing stressed. He explained: "To be realistic, we are not the Al-Ittihad we want to be, and we can't transform at the push of a button. We have to develop and work, as last season is not far away, and there were things that were not good. We are trying to develop everything, and we are still at the start of the journey, and we must work in order to return as quickly as possible."
 Admission of mistakes: Al Ain exploited Al-Ittihad's weaknesses
 Vissing was frustrated. His side knew they were up against an opponent with continental pedigree and plenty of quality, yet they made bright starts to both halves and had nothing to show for it.
 He said: "We feel great frustration after the defeat. We knew how difficult it would be to face a team with experience that has achieved big results, and we prepared for the match, but I think we started both the first and second halves well, and we could not translate our advantage into goals."
 The coach also took aim at the manner of some of the goals his team gave away. "The second goal was silly and we conceded it badly, and after we scored our goal, we gained confidence, but we conceded another goal in a silly way. We faced a clever team with good potential, and we were not at our best mentally, physically or technically," he added.
 Tiredness told in the end, as Vissing admitted when wrapping up. "Fatigue affected us, and we could not keep up with the opponent physically. I spoke to the players and told them that if we want to compete we must be better. This is a painful truth, and we must raise our heads and face it."
